title: CPAT Excel-AI
text:
CPAT Excel-AI


CPAT-AI overview: the mitigation prototypeStatus, how to run it, results (release 1.5) · PowerPoint, latest version
CPAT-AI: the pitchClimate policy analysis you can read, check and run fast; 8 slides · PowerPoint, latest version
Use of AI in climate fiscal toolsThe project: Excel-AI, Coded CPAT, other AI tools, timelines · PowerPoint, latest version

Excel-AI is CPAT rebuilt as readable Excel workbooks, generated and checked by AI. The modules (mitigation, distribution, air pollution; one workbook each, without macros, run from a Master workbook that holds every macro) cover the CPAT mitigation and distribution chain with plain, short formulas (one formula per block), open fast (values shipped, shared formulas, a binary .xlsb working copy), and are checked number for number by independent Python recomputation. The mitigation workbook opens on its Dashboard (country, policy scenario, key numbers and charts) and computes in numbered sections in sheet order; the Master runs many countries and scenarios and keeps the results. Rebuilding it found the legacy bugs counted in chapter 1, each fixed in the prototype and written up with a cell-level fix plan; every open modelling question is replicated and tracked.



Chapter
What it covers




1 Overview
Excel-AI, legacy CPAT as the reference, status, and the rule on bugs and issues


2 The mitigation module
The workbook: quick start through the Master, the Dashboard, the tabs, its sections in brief, results, limits, many scenarios, the data tabs


3 Other modules
The standalone distribution and air-pollution workbooks


4 Data and working practice
The data editions, files and releases, checks, the repository



The method of every block (prices, demand, power, road transport, emissions and the ETS, revenues and GDP, distribution), with its equations and pseudocode, is in the CPAT-AI Model tab, shared with CPAT Python: open it.
Chapter 2 is generated from the documents kept beside the code (excel_ai/mitigation/docs/) by make_qmd.py.

title: 1  Overview
text:
1.1 What Excel-AI is
Excel-AI is the Excel side of the CPAT-AI project: Excel prototypes of legacy CPAT, written by Python builders (openpyxl) and checked by LibreOffice recalculation and independent Python recomputation, for modellers and reviewers who work in Excel and for the CPAT team. Its files are in excel_ai/.

title: 1  Overview
text:
Modules. One workbook per module, without macros (since 1.2.0): mitigation (the integrated model), distribution and air pollution.
The Master workbook. excel_ai/master/CPAT-AI-MT_latest.xlsm (the MT, Multiscenario Tool; activated asexcel_ai/active_workbooks/CPAT-AI-MT.xlsb) holds every macro: it activates the modules (formulas to 2041, saved as .xlsb), updates their data tables (Power Query, the country or all countries) and the distribution inputs, runs every country with every scenario, keeps the results as values and compares them in tables and charts (Section 1.5).
Releases. Mitigation and the Master 1.5.1; Distribution 0.5.1, on its own 0.x line (0.1.0-0.1.4, then 0.2.0-0.2.3, 0.3.0, 0.4.0-0.4.2, 0.5.0-0.5.1, following the Mitigation releases 1.0.0 to 1.3.1). One line per release: excel_ai/core/CHANGELOG.md.
Inputs. The policy and parameter inputs are the rows and names of the legacy MTInputs sheet (NameOfParameter), in legacy units. The codes map (excel_ai/core/CPAT-AI_CodesMap_latest.xlsx, tab Inputs) lists every input with its row, its name, its legacy name and its Python key.
Codes and data. Input codes, output codes and the sector and fuel vocabularies are shared with the Python model (the CPAT Python tab), which replicates Excel-AI number for number. Both read the root folder data/ (Section 4.1).
The rule on bugs and issues (Section 1.6).

title: 1  Overview
text:
1.2 Legacy CPAT: the reference
The legacy workbook is the ground truth for both models. The latest version, 1.0pre_465, is kept read-only in data/ (the earlier NoPropData copies of 456, 459 and 465 are no longer in the repository):







File
Role




data/legacy/CPAT 1.0pre_465_Shell.xlsb
The legacy CPAT workbook with its six proprietary tabs empty (every other tab filled); the reference for input rows and names, and for the register’s cell references


data/Public01/legacy/CPAT 1.0pre_465_Public01.xlsb
The shell filled with data edition Public01’s tables (the proprietary ones perturbed)



The legacy workbook is never edited or re-saved; work is done on copies in scratch folders.

title: 1  Overview
text:
1.3 How the work proceeds

Replicate. A block of legacy CPAT is rebuilt in the prototype, formula by formula, with the same sections and the same codes.
Check. An independent Python recomputation of the block reproduces every number; the prototype’s result is compared with legacy’s stored results.
Classify every difference. A difference is either a legacy bug (fixed in the prototype, with a cell-level fix plan for legacy), a legacy issue (replicated and tracked), or a departure decided by the team (tracked).
Release. The builder writes a new version; the quick check, the paste test and the regression against the previous release must pass; the register documents, the tracker, the codes map and the decks are regenerated.
Port. Validated blocks are ported to the Python model (the CPAT Python tab).

title: 1  Overview
text:
1.5 How the workbooks work







File
What it is




excel_ai/master/CPAT-AI-MT_latest.xlsm (the MT, Multiscenario Tool; activated asexcel_ai/active_workbooks/CPAT-AI-MT.xlsb)
The Master: open it first (Excel 365, macros on). Tab Dashboard: the core macros, the countries and scenarios to run, the data choices; tab Activation and Macros: every other macro, explained, the module table and the data sources; the master scenario table and the stored results


excel_ai/<module>/<Name>_latest.xlsx
The latest unactivated module: no macros, formulas to 2035 (small, quick to open), with the values of the full model


excel_ai/active_workbooks/<Name>_latest.xlsb
The activated module, written by the Master: formulas to 2041, recalculated. Work here


excel_ai/<module>/releases/<Name>_v<version>.xlsx
Every version (to 1.1.0: <Name>-Prototype_v<version>.xlsm, with macros)


excel_ai/master/
The Master’s builder and its VBA (CPATMaster.bas)




Activate all. On the Master’s Dashboard, Activate all opens each module’s .xlsx (from the clone, else GitHub), copies the 2035 column across to 2041 in every scenario group of Mitigation and Outputs, adds the live scenario groups (four by default), writes the Master’s scenario table into the module, recalculates and saves <Name>_latest.xlsb next to the Master. Calculation is automatic.
Choose the countries and the scenarios on the Master’s Dashboard: one country per row and one scenario ID per row (BASE the baseline, P1-P5 the presets, U1, U2, … user scenarios; the IDs of the Master’s tab Scenarios, the rows of legacy MTInputs), and the data source and rows. Every country listed runs every scenario listed. Update data loads the linked data tabs by Power Query (all countries, for a run of many).
Run scenarios. The Master runs the list in batches over the live scenario groups 2-4 of the mitigation workbook (the baseline once per country; ETS scenarios with their goal seek, one per group) and stores every run as values in StoredResults.
Read the results. Live, in the mitigation workbook: tab Dashboard (the country and the policy scenario chosen by name, key numbers and charts), Outputs (the live scenario groups side by side, one output code per row, in Mitigation’s row order within each topic; code variable.sector.fuel.suffix, with the country in front and the scenario number at the end; cost components cost.<sector>.<fuel>.<component>) and Diagnostic (the country’s baseline). Stored, in the Master: StoredResults, Scenario comparison, OneCountry and ManyCountries. Tab Docs & Versions of the module holds the version log, the differences with legacy, the variable dictionary and the LAMBDAs.
Other macros (tab Activation and Macros): Send scenario to Mitigation, Get live scenario, Sync scenarios to Mitigation, Store live scenarios, Estimate run time, Goal-seek ETS price, Achieve NDCs, Distribution from Mitigation (the export block, section 11a, into the distribution workbook), Save results to .csv and others, each with what it does.

Speed. The modules ship with their calculated values and formulas to 2035, so they open quickly; repeated formulas are stored once as shared formulas; the activated workbook is a binary .xlsb; calculation is automatic.
Next steps. A user interface (its specification, a mock-up and the core graphs of country reports, is in excel_ai/bugs_and_legacy/ui_spec/); model settings split from policy inputs; the other modules (distribution started; air pollution; transport co-benefits); the full set of core graphs in the Master (which replaces the legacy Multiscenario Tool, kept in excel_ai/bugs_and_legacy/legacy_multiscenario_tool/); the real data behind the dummy panels of the Dashboard and the Diagnostic.
The .xlsb are generated files: on a git conflict take either side and activate again; never merge them, and never commit Excel’s ~$ lock files. A workbook run with real data stays on your local drive. The release notes are in the task log (excel_ai/core/CAVEATS.md). Details: Chapter 2 and Section 2.7.

title: 1  Overview
text:
1.6 Bugs and issues






ImportantThe rule



Never replicate a legacy bug; always replicate a legacy issue, and track it.


The rule applies to every model of the project, in Excel and in Python. It keeps the prototypes faithful to legacy CPAT where legacy does what it means to, and correct where it does not, and it makes every difference from legacy visible.

1.6.1 Definitions









Kind
Code
Meaning
What the prototype does




Legacy bug
L
Legacy does not compute what it means to: a wrong row, a double application, a dead reference
Fixes it, never replicates it; the fix is written up as a cell-level plan for legacy


Prototype bug
M
A bug found in the prototype itself
Fixes it and records it


Documentation bug
DOC
An error in the CPAT methodology documentation
Corrects it in the methodology’s chapter Corrections


Major issue, data
MId
One of the five most important data issues (MId1-MId5)
As an issue: replicates it and tracks it


Major issue, methodology
MIm
One of the five most important open questions of method (MIm1-MIm5)
As an issue: replicates it and tracks it


Issue
I
Legacy does what it means to, but the choice is open to question
Does the same as legacy and tracks it


Departure
LD
A deliberate difference from legacy that is not a bug fix
Kept only by decision of the team; tracked in the prototype’s LegacyDiff sheet


Upgrade
U
A feature beyond legacy
Tracked



The ten major issues were issues (I) first; the register keeps their former codes (MId1-MId5: I90, I97, I98, I91, I92; MIm1-MIm5: I71, I62, I31, I41, I113).
Data problems are issues. They are replicated. Where legacy needs a formula fix to handle the data correctly, that fix is a legacy bug (L) with a cell plan and the issue is ranked Very high; where no cell plan is possible, the prototype aligns with legacy exactly and the issue is ranked Extremely high.


1.6.2 The register
Every bug and issue lives in one register, the single source from which the documents are generated:







Document
What it holds




excel_ai/bugs_and_legacy/Legacy_CPAT_Bugs_v<version>.docx
The legacy bugs, each with its cell-level fix plan, and the data problems by priority


excel_ai/bugs_and_legacy/Tracking_Legacy_Bugs_v<version>.xlsx
The master list of bugs and issues, every module, in the same columns; shared with the CPAT team


excel_ai/core/BUGS.md, excel_ai/core/ISSUES.md
The two short lists


excel_ai/bugs_and_legacy/register/Legacy_CPAT_Register.json
The register as data



The register is written in excel_ai/bugs_and_legacy/register/issues_register.py and register.py; make_documentation.py regenerates every document from it at each release.


1.6.3 Current counts


261 legacy bugs, 27 prototype bugs, 21 documentation bugs. Legacy 465: 52 fixed (confirmed), 9 fixed with caveats, 2 marked fixed but not fixed, 198 open. Legacy 468 (1.9.10): 8 more fixed, 9 fixed with caveats, 192 open. (register v1.9.40, excel_ai/core/BUGS.md)
10 major issues (5 data, MId; 5 methodology, MIm), 158 other issues, 14 data problems (the MId among them), 9 major differences (MD), 37 departures (LegacyDiff), 15 upgrades. (register v1.9.40, excel_ai/core/ISSUES.md)

The status Legacy 465 records whether the CPAT team has fixed each bug in the latest legacy workbook; each claimed fix is checked against the workbook (excel_ai/bugs_and_legacy/fixes/check465/).


1.6.4 Priorities
Issues and data problems are ranked so the most urgent are seen first: Extremely high and Very high for data problems (as defined above), then Major and Minor. Bugs carry High, Medium or Low by their effect on results.

title: 2  The mitigation module
text:
2.1 What it is
Source: excel_ai/mitigation/docs/Documentation.md.
The guide to the mitigation workbook: what it is, how to run it, how it works section by section, its results and its limits. The method of every block, with its equations and pseudocode, is in the website’s CPAT-AI Model tab; every legacy bug and issue is in the bug book and the tracker. This guide describes release 1.5 (Mitigation and Master 1.5.1, Distribution 0.5.1).
The mitigation module of the IMF/World Bank Climate Policy Assessment Tool (CPAT), rebuilt as one readable Excel workbook for one country at a time.
It answers one question: what do carbon pricing and related policies do to energy prices, energy use, emissions, government revenue, GDP and welfare, year by year to 2041?

title: 2  The mitigation module
text:
Policies in: carbon tax, a new emissions trading system (ETS) with a cap, feebates, fuel excises, fuel subsidy and price-control reform, a methane fee, existing carbon pricing, power-sector policies, and road-vehicle policies (with the engineer road model).
Results out: retail energy prices, fuel use in 16 sectors and 9 fuels, electricity generation, investment and prices, revenue, CO₂ and the other greenhouse gases, local air pollutants, GDP effects, the gap to the country’s NDC, welfare, and the exports that the distribution and air-pollution modules read. Household effects by decile are the separate Distribution module.
One country, any country: no formula contains a country’s number or name. Every country value comes from the data tabs, looked up by the country chosen on tab Dashboard. The shipped data are complete for Egypt.
Same as legacy, minus its bugs: it follows legacy CPAT except where legacy has a bug (fixed) or an open question (an issue, replicated and tracked). See section 6.
Readable and checked: every formula is short (target 90 characters, at most 115), and one formula serves a whole block of cells. An independent Python recomputation (CPAT Python) checks the numbers.
Fast: the workbook ships with its calculated values and formulas to 2035, so it opens quickly; repeated formulas are stored once as shared formulas; the Master saves the working copy as a binary .xlsb. Calculation is automatic.

title: 2  The mitigation module
text:
2.2 Quick start
The module workbooks have no macros. Every macro is in the Master workbook, excel_ai/master/CPAT-AI-MT_latest.xlsm (its Activate all saves it into the git-ignored excel_ai/active_workbooks/ as CPAT-AI-MT.xlsb, where you then work). The mitigation module ships as excel_ai/mitigation/CPAT-AI-Mitigation_latest.xlsx (every version in excel_ai/mitigation/releases/); the Master activates it into the workbook you work in, excel_ai/active_workbooks/CPAT-AI-Mitigation_latest.xlsb.

Get the files. Keep a clone of the repository up to date (git, or the SyncRepo script). The Master finds the modules in the clone, or else downloads them from GitHub.
Open the Master in Excel 365 and enable macros. If the file was downloaded, unblock it first (file Properties > Unblock). It opens on tab Dashboard, which has the three core macros: Activate all, Run scenarios and Update data. Every other macro is on tab Activation and Macros, one button each, with what it does.
Activate all. The Master opens each module’s .xlsx, copies the 2035 column of every scenario group across to 2041, adds the live scenario groups (four by default: the baseline and three scenarios), writes its scenario table into the module, recalculates and saves CPAT-AI-Mitigation_latest.xlsb next to itself. Activate again whenever a new .xlsx arrives.
Choose the countries and the scenarios on the Master’s Dashboard. Type one country per row in the Countries list and one scenario ID per row in the Scenario list (both grow downwards). The IDs are those of the Master’s tab Scenarios: BASE the baseline, P1-P3 the presets (P1 carbon price $20/tCO2 from 2027, P2 Package A, P3 carbon price $50/tCO2), P4 an extra (Package B, an ETS on power and industry), U1, U2, … your own scenarios. Every country listed runs every scenario listed. Choose the data source and the rows to load (one country or all) beside the buttons.
Update data if you run more than one country or need a fresher source: the Master loads the linked data tabs by Power Query, once for all countries.
Run scenarios. The Master runs every country with every scenario, in batches over the live scenario groups 2-4 of the mitigation workbook (the baseline once per country). An ETS scenario gets its goal seek, one per group. Each run is stored as values in tab StoredResults. Estimate run time (on the other tab) says how long a run will take.
Read the results.

Live, in the mitigation workbook: tab Dashboard (the country and the scenarios of groups 2-4, key numbers and charts with the four scenarios), tab Comparison (the live scenarios side by side in a chosen year), tab Output Data (every live scenario group side by side, one output code per row), tabs Climate and Fiscal.
Stored, in the Master: StoredResults (one row per output per run), Scenario comparison (the key indicators of up to ten runs in a chosen year, against the first), OneCountry (one country, several scenarios, as time series) and ManyCountries (several countries, one scenario, one year).

Look at one scenario live. On the mitigation workbook’s Dashboard, choose the country and the scenarios of groups 2-4 by their short label (tab Pre-defined row 2, e.g. Carbon tax $20, Tax to $50 + feebates; group 1 is the baseline); the full name shows on a grey line under each picker. A scenario group pasted by hand is read wherever it starts (found by its header “Scenario: output code” in row 1); the note at the top of Mitigation says which columns to copy and where to paste, and a red line on the Dashboard says when a group is not at its column. To change a policy, edit its column on tab Scenarios (the rows of legacy MTInputs; for example CPLevelTarget, the carbon price in the target year). In the Master: Send scenario to Mitigation puts a Master scenario into group 2; Get live scenario adds group 2 to the Master’s table as the next user scenario; Sync scenarios to Mitigation writes the whole table into the module.
Distribution. Distribution from Mitigation (other tab) copies the export block of the activated mitigation workbook (section 11a) into the activated distribution workbook, recalculates and saves it.

Good practice. The .xlsb files are generated: on a git conflict take either side and activate again; never merge them, and never commit Excel’s ~$ lock files. A workbook run with real (non-public) data stays on your local drive.

title: 2  The mitigation module
text:
2.4 How it works
The Mitigation tab runs top to bottom, one section per step, numbered 1 to 19 in sheet order. Each section starts with a band (its number and title), ends with a summary row (the only row shown when the sheet is rolled up) and has sub-blocks with headings. Every row carries a code in columns A:C (variable, fuel, sector); its label, unit and source come from the variable dictionary.
Each scenario is a group of columns: group 1 the baseline (scenario 1), group 2 the Dashboard’s policy scenario, groups 3 and 4 two more scenarios (added at activation; the Master’s runs use groups 2-4). Inputs that are the same for every scenario (the results year, some power and data settings) are read from scenario 1’s column and checked on Settings.

The method of each block, with its equations and pseudocode, is in the website’s CPAT-AI Model tab (https://cpmodelai.github.io/docs/#model; sources docs/CPAT_model_documentation_qmd/), shared with CPAT Python. The notes in excel_ai/mitigation/docs/methods/ are the workbook-side detail: rows, names and checks.

2.4.1 Policies (section 2)
Each policy is a path from a start year to a target year, set per scenario on Scenarios. The carbon price follows that path:
τ(t) = path(t; start year, target year, start level, target level) · (CPI index if the inputs are nominal)
A new ETS starts at a price estimate and is checked against its cap; the Master’s goal seek refines it. Feebates act through a shadow price, which changes efficiency but raises no revenue. Existing carbon taxes and ETS prices come from the World Bank Carbon Pricing Dashboard data. Where the chosen main scenario is a regulation, the carbon price path becomes a shadow price on the efficiency margin.


2.4.2 Energy prices (section 3)
For each fuel and sector, the retail price builds up from the international price:
supply cost  C(t) = fixed part + (C(t−1) − fixed part) · international price(t) / international price(t−1)
retail price R    = (C + excise and other taxes) · (1 + VAT)
after policy P    = R + new carbon tax + ETS price + new excise, each with VAT
Subsidies are negative taxes; subsidy and price-control phase-outs add a wedge. Historical prices come from the price data up to the last historical year; later years are projected. A memo at the end of the section gives average prices and price indices.


2.4.3 Power (section 4)
Electricity demand comes from the sectors. The power model, as legacy’s engineer model, decides each year:

Dispatch: which plants run, by their variable cost (fuel, carbon price, operation).
Investment: new capacity by technology, chosen by levelised cost with a logit share, within scale-up limits.
Prices: electricity prices from the cost of generation, with taxes, subsidies and price controls.

Power-sector policies (no new coal, nuclear from a year, renewable subsidies, power purchase agreements, rebating revenue, an electricity excise) are set per scenario.


2.4.4 Energy demand (sections 5 to 10)
Fuel use in each sector changes each year with income, its own price and efficiency:
Q(t) = Q(t−1) · (efficiency gain) · (1 + GDP growth)^(income elasticity) · (P(t)/P(t−1))^(price elasticity) · (efficiency response to prices)
The elasticities are legacy CPAT’s. By default road fuel use follows these elasticities as every other sector. With TrModel = Engineer, the road engineer model of section 5 replaces it: vehicle stocks by class, cost of ownership, the choice between combustion and electric vehicles, and vehicle policies (feebates, EV subsidies, purchase taxes, distance tax). Section 5 is computed in every scenario either way, so the two approaches can be compared. In the buildings section, a block moves part of the most-used cooking fuel to biomass when its price rises (leakage). Section 10 adds up fuel use by sector and fuel, including the fuel burnt in power plants.
Fuels. The nine fuels (coal, gas, gasoline, diesel, LPG, kerosene, jet fuel, other oil products, biomass) are one list in the builder (FUELS in build.py): every block of every subsector, the emission-factor and air-pollutant lookups and every total follow it. A new fuel is added there (with the price build-up it uses and, until the data have its own rows, the fuel whose data it reads), not by copying rows in the workbook: a copied row reads the wrong rows of the parallel blocks.


2.4.5 Exports to the other modules (sections 11 and 15)
Sections with a blue band hold what other modules read, by code. Section 11 comes right after energy consumption: block 11a (defined name ExportDistn) is the input of the Distribution module (household effects by decile in one analysis year). The Master copies it into the distribution workbook (Distribution from Mitigation). Block 11b holds the outputs of the road model (section 5) for the transport co-benefits module. Section 15, the local air pollutants, is what the air-pollution module will read.


2.4.6 Revenues (section 12)
Revenue is fuel use times the tax per unit, by fuel and sector, for existing taxes, existing subsidies (negative) and new policies:
revenue from new policies = fuel use · (carbon tax + excise + auctioned share · ETS price + VAT on them)
total revenue             = existing taxes + subsidies + new policies + methane fee
The power sector adds its own revenue and subsidies. Feebates are revenue neutral.


2.4.7 Emissions (sections 13 to 15)
CO₂ = fuel use · emission factor        (factors calibrated to the GHG inventory where the switch is on)
The other greenhouse gases (methane, nitrous oxide, F-gases) follow their drivers; methane from fuel supply responds to the methane fee. The NDC block compares the scenario with the country’s chosen NDC target. Local air pollutants (fine particles, sulphur and nitrogen oxides and others) are fuel use times pollutant factors.


2.4.8 GDP, carbon pricing, welfare (sections 16 to 19)
New revenue is fiscal space. How it is used (tax cuts, investment, transfers) moves GDP through fiscal multipliers, from the following year:
fiscal space fs(t)  = (new revenue in the scenario − in the baseline) / GDP
GDP effect          = Σ over uses: share of the use · Σ over lags (change in fs · multiplier of the use)
The GDP effect feeds back into GDP growth (section 1), which drives fuel use. Section 17 reports carbon prices, coverage, the effective carbon rate, and the Total Carbon Price (price signals per tonne weighted by CO2) and Total Effective Carbon Price (the same signals weighted by the emission cut from a uniform carbon tax; a uniform 1 USD/tCO2 tax adds 1 to both). Section 18 reads the damages per unit of fuel from the air-pollution and transport co-benefits modules; section 19 values the climate damages avoided, the efficiency costs and the co-benefits, and gives the efficient prices with their cost components.

title: 2  The mitigation module
text:
2.5 Results
Outputs shows the key results of every scenario group side by side, in the columns of the scenario groups of Mitigation (row 5: the scenario number of each group). It lists only what the prototype computes, by topic in the order of Mitigation’s sections, and within a topic in Mitigation’s row order: policies, energy prices, power, energy use, revenue and fiscal, emissions and NDC, air pollution, macroeconomy, efficient prices and their cost components, welfare and externalities.
Output codes. Each row carries a code built from its parts, <module>.<variable>.<sector>.<fuel>[.<suffix>] (columns B and D:G). The full code adds the country in front and the scenario number at the end: for example egy.mit.co2.tot.tot.2 is Egypt’s total CO₂ from fuel combustion in scenario 2. The cost components of the efficient prices are coded cost.<sector>.<fuel>.<component>. The names come from the same dictionary as Mitigation’s labels. The codes are those of CPAT Python; the codes map excel_ai/core/CPAT-AI_CodesMap_v<version>.xlsx lists the code protocol, the vocabularies, the variables, the output codes and every input (its MTInputs row, its name and its Python key).
Dashboard, Comparison, Climate and Fiscal show the key numbers and charts of the live scenarios, read from Output Data by code. Some of their panels still hold dummy data (pale orange) until the data or the other modules deliver them (household impacts by decile, household energy spending). The effective carbon rates by sector (Diagnostic) are model rows of section 17; the averted deaths (Dashboard) are an interim estimate from the value of averted ambient PM2.5 over a value of a statistical life (section 18), until the air-pollution module computes deaths.
Stored results are in the Master: StoredResults (values, one row per output per run, keyed by country, scenario ID and code; tab Indicators chooses which rows a run stores), Scenario comparison, OneCountry and ManyCountries (tables and charts read from StoredResults). Save results to .csv writes StoredResults to a file. Details: Running many scenarios.

title: 2  The mitigation module
text:
2.6 Limits and differences from legacy
The rule: never replicate a legacy bug; always replicate a legacy issue, and track it. A bug is legacy computing what it does not intend; the prototype fixes it. An issue is legacy doing what it means to, where the choice is open to question; the prototype does the same. Problems of the input data are issues too: where legacy reads the data wrongly, the formula fix is a bug with a cell plan and the issue is Very high; where no cell plan is possible, the prototype does exactly what legacy does and the issue is Extremely high.







Code
Kind




L
Legacy bug: fixed in the prototype, with a cell-level fix plan for legacy


M
Prototype bug: fixed and recorded


DOC
Error in the CPAT methodology documentation: corrected in its chapter Corrections


MId
Major issue, data (MId1-MId5): the most important data problems


MIm
Major issue, methodology (MIm1-MIm5): the most important open questions of method


I
Issue: replicated and tracked


LD
Departure from legacy decided by the team (listed on Docs & Versions)


U
Upgrade beyond legacy



The ten major issues keep their former issue codes in the register. The bugs, with the cell-level fix for legacy CPAT and the status of each in the latest legacy file CPAT 1.0pre_465, are in the bug book excel_ai/bugs_and_legacy/Legacy_CPAT_Bugs_v<version>.docx; the master list of bugs and issues is the tracker excel_ai/bugs_and_legacy/Tracking_Legacy_Bugs_v<version>.xlsx; the short lists are excel_ai/core/BUGS.md and excel_ai/core/ISSUES.md.
Limits.

Data: the shipped data are Egypt’s, with the six proprietary tables perturbed (data edition Public01). Other countries need their data loaded through the Master (issue MId1).
Other modules: the air-pollution and transport co-benefits values on FromAP and FromTrans are typed for Egypt only, until those modules write them. The distribution module runs one scenario at a time. Achieve NDCs and the ETS goal seek of the Master’s runs await the team’s test in Excel.
Settings and policies: some inputs on Scenarios are read from scenario 1 for every scenario (a check on Settings shows them); model settings and policy inputs are not yet separated.
Legacy row numbers in the method notes are rows of CPAT 1.0pre_456_NoPropData.xlsb, the file the prototype was built against; in CPAT 1.0pre_465 the Mitigation rows from 5667 on sit 11 to 15 rows higher. The input tab Scenarios has the rows of the 465 MTInputs.
Not built: a few legacy features (upgrades U), the air-pollution calculations and the transport co-benefits module.

Next steps. (The user interface, tab User-defined, and the split of model settings from policy inputs were done in 1.9.35-1.9.41.) the other modules (distribution started, air pollution, transport co-benefits); the full set of core graphs in the Master; the real data behind the dummy panels of Dashboard and Diagnostic.

title: 2  The mitigation module
text:
2.7 Running many scenarios
Source: excel_ai/mitigation/docs/methods/Macro_and_results.md.
Equations: Equations.md; workbook formulas: Formulas.md.
The mitigation workbook calculates four scenarios at a time, one group of columns each: group 1 is the baseline (scenario 1), group 2 the policy scenario chosen by name on tab Dashboard, groups 3 and 4 two more scenarios (added by the Master at activation). The macros and the stored results are in the Master workbook (excel_ai/master/CPAT-AI-MT_latest.xlsm (the MT, Multiscenario Tool; activated asexcel_ai/active_workbooks/CPAT-AI-MT.xlsb)); the module workbooks have no macros. The Master’s run sends the scenarios to the live groups 2-4 in batches, lets the workbook calculate and stores the results as values, which are compared afterwards. This follows the legacy Multiscenario Tool, where every country listed runs every scenario listed and the outputs are stored.

2.7.1 Where things are







Place
What it holds




Dashboard (mitigation workbook)
The country and the policy scenario of Mitigation group 2, chosen by its name from tab Pre-defined (Scenarios before 1.9.41; PolicyName; its number PolicyScen); key numbers and charts of the live scenarios.


Cover (mitigation workbook)
The live scenario groups at activation (LiveGroups, 2, 3 or 4; default 4), the scenarios of groups 3 and 4 by name (DashG3, DashG4), the data transfer choices, the status written by the Master.


Scenarios, column G
Scenario 1, the baseline (ID BASE).


Scenarios, columns H onwards
One column per scenario definition: short name (row 2, the legend in the charts), number (row 5), name (row 6), ID (row 7: P1-P5 the presets, U1, U2, … user scenarios), then the inputs, in the rows of legacy MTInputs. The last three columns (AX-AZ) are the Master’s run columns: a batch writes its scenarios there.


Mitigation
Scenario groups side by side: group 1 the baseline, group 2 the policy scenario of the Dashboard, groups 3 and 4 further scenarios; group n calculates the scenario number in its row 5.


Outputs
The key results of every scenario group side by side, in the columns of Mitigation’s groups: only what the prototype computes, by topic in the order of Mitigation’s sections and, within a topic, in Mitigation’s row order (the revenue of every fuel included); columns A:J the output code (variable.sector.fuel.suffix, built from the parts in D:G), module, legacy MTOutputs code(s), indicator, unit and Mitigation row; row 5 the scenario number of each group. Each cell is Mitigation’s cell of its code in the same column.


Master: Dashboard
The core macros (Activate all, Run scenarios, Update data), the data source and the rows to load, the Countries and Scenario lists (from row 18, growing downwards), the scenario shown with its key inputs, the run status.


Master: Scenarios
The master copy of the scenario table (the module’s rows, the IDs in row 7). Activation and Sync scenarios write it into the module by ID and NameOfParameter.


Master: Indicators
The rows of Outputs and whether a run stores them (Include = Yes / No).


Master: StoredResults
Results as values only, vertical as the legacy MTOutputs: one row per output per run, keyed by country code, scenario ID and code stem, with when, from which version and which data source it was stored; an index of the stored runs on the right.


Master: Scenario comparison, OneCountry, ManyCountries
Tables and charts read from StoredResults by key: up to ten runs in a chosen year against the first; one country’s scenarios as time series; several countries’ runs of one scenario in one year, against each country’s BASE.


Master: VBA module CPATMaster
Every macro (source excel_ai/master/CPATMaster.bas).

The short label (tab Scenarios row 2; at most 28 characters, unique, checked in row 4) names a scenario in the pickers, chart legends and tables; the full name shows on a grey line under each Dashboard picker and Scenario comparison header.
Paths continue after their target year as set in the model: the carbon price follows its Scenarios switch, and feebates are held at their target rate (as legacy; L174 fixed).


2.7.3 Main scenario choice and regulations as shadow prices (LD9)
Scenarios row 13 (ScenarioSelected, ” - Carbon tax” in every shipped scenario) picks a row of the legacy scenario table (legacy Mitigation rows 222-262, columns N:AC; sheet Mapping, block “Main scenarios”): whether the scenario prices carbon explicitly (legacy row 259), its efficiency adjustment (Scenarios rows 247-251) and the sectors its shadow price covers (rows 240-257).

Explicit scenarios (carbon tax, total carbon price, coal excise, road fuel tax, electricity emissions tax and excise): the carbon price path of Scenarios rows 18-21 is the carbon tax (cpx = cptraj), as before.
Shadow-pricing scenarios (feebates, power supply feebates, energy efficiency regulations, power feebate, vehicle fuel economy, residential and industrial efficiency regulations; and “Baseline”): no explicit carbon tax (cpx = 0); the carbon price path becomes a shadow price on the efficiency margin, reg.<sector> = cp.shd x the scenario’s adjustment (energy efficiency 247, vehicle fuel economy 248, residential 249, industrial 250, feebates 251; Egypt 0.7, feebates 1) x 1 if the scenario covers the sector. It enters shpx (with the feebate part, now x row 251, and the ETS benchmark part), so fuel use responds through efficiency only, and power through shk (legacy bugs L87, L88 fixed: legacy’s regulation share is 0 and never reaches power).
The road vehicle feebate of the engineer road model adds reg.rod (the road regulation shadow price) instead of the carbon price, which is in the fuel price already (prototype bug M13).
A text that is not in the table counts as explicit pricing (as the shipped ” - Carbon tax”).



2.7.4 Macros (in the Master)
Run scenarios is the button of the MT’s (the Master’s) tab Dashboard; Activate all and Update data, with their settings, and every other macro have one button each, with what it does, on tab Activation and Macros (1.9.5) (also Alt+F8). Calculation is automatic in the modules and is switched back on after every macro, even one that stops.

Activate all (or Mitigation, Distribution or Air pollution only): opens the module’s latest .xlsx (the local repository copy, else its GitHub link), copies the 2035 column of every scenario group across to 2041 (Mitigation and Outputs), adds the live groups 3 and 4 (as LiveGroups says), writes the Master’s scenario table into tab Scenarios, recalculates and saves <Name>_latest.xlsb in excel_ai/active_workbooks/. The workbook stays open.
Update data: refreshes the linked data tabs of the activated mitigation workbook by Power Query, from the source and the rows chosen on the Master’s Dashboard (the module’s Cover can override), and saves the workbook.
Run scenarios: every country of the Dashboard’s list with every scenario of its list. Countries without data are reported before the run starts. Per country: the country is set, the baseline (the Master’s BASE) is stored once, and the other scenarios are sent by NameOfParameter to the run columns in batches of three, one per live group 2-4, with one recalculation per batch. A batch with an ETS scenario runs the goal seek on every such group at once. Each run is stored in StoredResults (the rows with Include = Yes). The Dashboard shows the progress and the measured run time; at the end the module’s dashboard, scenario 1, the ETS overrides and the calculation mode are restored, and the results are written to a .csv when the Dashboard says Yes.
Estimate run time: times one full recalculation and estimates the run of the Dashboard’s lists.
Store live scenarios: stores every live group of Output Data (Outputs before 1.9.40) in StoredResults, under the module’s country and the scenario IDs of its tab Pre-defined (Scenarios before 1.9.41).
Sync scenarios to Mitigation, Send scenario to Mitigation, Get live scenario: write the Master’s scenario table into the module; send the scenario shown on the Dashboard into group 2; add group 2’s scenario to the Master’s table as the next user scenario.
Goal-seek ETS price (live) and Achieve NDCs (live): the ETS price path that meets the cap of group 2’s scenario; the carbon tax of group 2’s scenario scaled until GHG emissions meet the NDC target in the target year.
Distribution from Mitigation: copies the export block of Mitigation (section 11a, defined name ExportDistn) into FromMitigation of the activated distribution workbook, by code (it stops if the rows do not match), recalculates and saves it.
Clear results, Save results to .csv, Indicators: include all / key only: empty StoredResults (after a confirmation); write it to a file; choose the rows a run stores.

The ETS goal seek is legacy’s damped log-space iteration, as in ets_goalseek.py. It starts from the override prices, or from the fast estimate if there are none. Each step is p × (proposed price / p) ^ alpha, mixed 0.3 with the previous iterate, with 5% smoothing. Alpha halves when the error grows (minimum 0.0625) and rises ×1.2 when the error more than halves (maximum 1). It stops when the worst |covered / cap − 1| is below 0.5%, or after 20 iterations.


2.7.5 Comparing and keeping results

Live (in the mitigation workbook): Outputs holds the four scenario groups side by side; the Dashboard and the Diagnostic chart them.
Stored (in the Master): StoredResults keeps every run as values, so runs of many countries and scenarios sit together. Scenario comparison compares up to ten stored runs in a chosen year with the first (level, difference and % difference, the last for strictly positive levels only) with a column chart; OneCountry shows one country’s scenarios as time series; ManyCountries shows several countries’ runs of one scenario in one year, against each country’s baseline.



2.7.6 Limits

Four live groups: a run of more scenarios goes in batches of three, each batch a recalculation.
Outputs defines what can be stored: its rows, each code once. To store more, add rows to Outputs (in the builder).
Many countries need every country’s data loaded once first (Update data, all countries).
The runs and the ETS goal seek of a run are checked in LibreOffice; Achieve NDCs is not yet tested; the team’s test in Excel is open.

title: 2  The mitigation module
text:
2.8 The data tabs
Source: excel_ai/mitigation/docs/methods/Data_tabs.md.
User request (2026-10-17): align the data tabs with legacy CPAT (grouped by module, legacy order, legacy names and content where possible, without undoing principled decisions); check that the model would work with the full all-country data; put every Egypt-only table alone on its tab or at the bottom; check how far the legacy data tables can be copied in. Then (same day): align more fully, going with the recommendations. The norm is NORMS.md 1.5.

2.8.1 Summary

Order. The data tabs sit under the legacy dividers in legacy order: DATA_MITIGATION->> (the tables derived for Mitigation last: CookingFuel, Multipliers, BaselineCO2; 1.2.2), DATA_DISTN->> (the distribution workbook), DATA_TRAN->>.
Copy-in rules (NORMS 1.5).

L, a single legacy table: the table itself, unchanged (same columns, column letters and codes; header row 3, data from A4; a key formula column right of the table where legacy has no unique key). Paste the legacy data rows at A4. 17 tabs: Balances, EnergyCons, CH4Inputs, UNPop, OilProductShares (v0.4.12), WEO, EF_GHG, SCC, EF_PM, IO_GTAP, HHSurvey, HH_Elast, ASPIRE, WHOCooking, GDPRatios, Transport1, Transport2.

Paste the legacy tab from row 3. 10 tabs: Countries, Elasticities, ETS+LTS, Multipliers, Prices_int, ECP, Transport3 (stored results, rows 5+) and, since v0.4.7, Power, CoC and GHGs (the inventory and, rows 1201-1388, the 2023-2024 emission shocks of the power model).
**L*, Prices_dom:** legacy header rows and codes; paste legacy rows 4 onwards at A1.

Country selection is a data step (NORMS 1.5, rule 2c). What legacy Mitigation computes from these tabs for the selected country sits in blocks of the Inputs tab, by formula, under the keys the model already used:

Inputs_ela: elasticities (the country’s column of Elasticities, as legacy column G);
Inputs_mult: multipliers (median ± standard deviation by group, instrument and lag);
Inputs_macro: GDP growth and levels, deflators, exchange rate (WEO series with legacy’s extension past the last data year, rows 417-467) and the energy trade balance and share traded (rows 741-743, from Balances);
Inputs_pint: international price series by source (rows 633-695);
Inputs_ecp: existing carbon pricing (rows 1675-1764; v0.4.12: carbon tax with single and fuel rates, national ETS and EU ETS, each code looked up in its own legacy block of ECP, coverage by data year, and two tables by ECP sector and fuel: carbon tax and ETS in $/tCO2);
Inputs_ef: CO2 emission factors (rows 980-1011);
Inputs_nc (v0.9.0): non-CO2 combustion emission factors of local pollutants and CH4 by legacy EF code (rows 1052-1663: country, else World Bank region, else world, from the all-country EF_PM; other energy the maximum across the other subsectors);
v0.4.7, power (legacy section 4, rows 2954-4300): Inputs_pset (the power settings of Scenarios scenario 1 and derived values, each a defined name Ps…), Inputs_ptech (one row per generation type, the former PowerTech: country, else world parameters, efficiency and generation from Balances, WACC from CoC, capacity factors), Inputs_ppath (year paths, the former PowerPaths: capex time factors, storage, income factor, fuel price shocks, prices) and Inputs_ppar (parameters, the former PowerParams). The chains are mapped in chapter Power. The Egypt values reproduce legacy’s cached values (macro series to 1e-15; power data to 1e-12), apart from one legacy bug fixed (L51: the coal trade balance was valued at the oil price) and one stale value in legacy’s stored run (I38: the wind and solar capex time factors for 2039-2041 differ from the legacy Power cells they reference; the prototype follows the Power tab).

Proprietary tables. The public legacy file (CPAT 1.0pre_456_NoPropData.xlsb) holds Egypt only in Balances, EnergyCons (empty), Prices_dom, EF_PM, IO_GTAP, HHSurvey, ASPIRE, WHOCooking, CalVal and Tran_Scatter. The model uses the first eight; all eight paste in directly.
All-country test: PASS. check_allcountry.py clones every Egypt row of every single-table tab under a dummy country (XEG) at the bottom of its table, renames Egypt’s codes to XEG in place on the tabs kept at legacy addresses, selects XEG and recalculates: no error values, every output of Mitigation and Distribution identical to Egypt’s.
No table from legacy’s cached Egypt run is left (v0.4.7). The former PowerTech, PowerPaths and PowerParams are computed from the legacy tabs on Inputs. BaselineCO2 (the scenario-1 CO2 the calibration uses) is derived by the build.
Legacy bugs in the power data: all fixed (v0.4.10, NORMS 0; v0.4.7 still copied them): L52 every generation type takes the country parameters where they exist (Egypt: solar fixed O&M 11.831 instead of 15 $/kW/y); L53 the actual capacity factor of the base year (installed capacity, Power rows 358-1635) is used inside the CFOverride bounds (Egypt: gas 0.385, wind 0.436, solar 0.347, hydro 0.592; base-year gas capacity 52 GW instead of 35); L54 hydro invests from the base year only when its generation share is above 50% (Egypt: from 2030); L55 the country rows are looked up in the country block first (China, Japan, Korea); L56 countries without CoC risk data take the default WACC, flagged.
Balances, EnergyCons, EF_PM, IO_GTAP, HHSurvey, HH_Elast, ASPIRE, WHOCooking and GDPRatios became legacy tables (v0.4.5). Then GHGs, CH4Inputs, UNPop, EF_GHG, SCC, Transport1 and Transport2 followed. The tables come from extract_legacy_tables.py, which writes legacy_<Tab>.csv verbatim from the legacy file (today into the legacy-form cache .buildcache/legacy_csv/<edition>/, saved to data/<edition>/tidy/ by data/scripts/legacy_csv.py).
Base-year fuel use and power demand now come from Balances through legacy’s flow mapping (Mapping columns J-M), as legacy does with BalancesOrConsumption = Balances; the old PowerDemand tab was dropped.
CO2 emission factors: the legacy EF_GHG table replaces the Egypt factors copied from legacy’s run. The selection of legacy Mitigation rows 980-1011 is now a data step on Inputs, and it reproduces the Egypt factors exactly:

the country’s code, else its World Bank region, else the world;
LPG and kerosene in power, and coal, LPG, kerosene and other oil products in road, take the row legacy points to;

All named ranges over data tables reach the capacity of the full legacy tables, with margin.

The values reproduce the former tables, except the wind and solar capex time factors for 2039-2041 (I94). title: 3  Other modules
text:
3.1 Distribution module
The mitigation module is the integrated model. Two further modules are standalone workbooks that take their inputs from it: the distribution module and the air-pollution module. Like Mitigation they have no macros: the Master workbook activates them into excel_ai/active_workbooks/ and carries values between them (Section 1.5).
The distribution module (version 0.5.1, on its own 0.x version line; excel_ai/distribution/CPAT-AI-Distribution_latest.xlsx, activated as excel_ai/active_workbooks/CPAT-AI-Distribution_latest.xlsb; every version in excel_ai/distribution/releases/) computes the household effects by decile of a mitigation scenario: price changes, budget shares, direct and indirect effects, revenue recycling and welfare. Its method is explained in the CPAT-AI Model tab (Distribution).
One copy of the formulas. The mitigation workbook does not hold the Distribution tab. The module is cut from a full build of the mitigation builder (CPAT_WITH_DIST=1): its tabs Cover (with the Master’s status), Scenarios (distribution rows shown), FromMitigation, Distribution, Settings, Mappings and the distribution data tabs. To change a formula, change the mitigation builder, then rebuild Mitigation and the module.
One input tab. Its only input from Mitigation is the tab FromMitigation: the values of the mitigation export block (section 11, block 11a, defined name ExportDistn; blue band), in the Mitigation column layout. The Master’s Update Distribution from Mitigation copies them from the activated mitigation workbook into the activated distribution workbook, by code (it stops if the rows do not match, for example two different versions), recalculates and saves it. The module runs one scenario at a time: the policy scenario of Mitigation group 2.
Build and check.
The check confirms that the Distribution tab equals a full build of the mitigation builder cell for cell, that FromMitigation equals block 11a through the macro’s row mapping, that no formula reads a dropped tab or an undefined name, and, end to end, that a carbon price changed in Mitigation and carried over by the update gives the same Distribution.

title: 3  Other modules
text:
cd excel_ai/distribution
python build_distribution.py    # the module, about 4 minutes
python check_distribution.py    # about 4 minutes

title: 3  Other modules
text:
3.2 Air-pollution module
The air-pollution module (excel_ai/air_pollution/) is a standalone rebuild of the Air Pollution module of legacy CPAT 1.0pre_459. It starts from the pollutant emissions produced by Mitigation (section 15, the export to the air pollution module, blue band) and does not recalculate fuel use or emissions.
Boundary. The inputs are the baseline and policy emission series keyed by the codes aps.<pollutant>.<sector>, with year, country, unit, scenario and source traceability. In legacy 459 the handoff is country.mit.em.<pollutant>.<sector>.<scenario> in tonnes per year; the current Mitigation outputs are in kt, so units are converted explicitly at the boundary. Once the input block is filled, the workbook runs without links to another workbook.
Scope. The module reproduces the calculations and options of legacy 459: emissions to concentrations, exposure and health burden, and economic outputs, for baseline and policy scenarios and their difference. Fuel externalities are reported as outputs only and are not fed back into Mitigation prices.
Status. The current workbook holds the scaffold: Cover, Data Sources, Mitigation Inputs and the nine public reference tables extracted from legacy 459 (the ap459_* tables of data/Public01/tidy/). The calculations, unit conversion, outputs and the numerical regression are open. The first regression case is Senegal, the country selected in the legacy NoPropData dashboard.
Validation. Each selected output is compared with legacy 459 by scenario and year, and every difference is classified as a confirmed bug fix, a replicated issue, or unresolved. Numerical equivalence is not claimed until the selected country has populated, reproducible inputs.

title: 3  Other modules
text:
3.3 Road transport co-benefits
The mitigation module reads the road-transport co-benefits as values typed on its tab FromTrans, as it reads the air-pollution marginal damages on FromAP (both typed for Egypt only: 0 for other countries, and row 1 of each tab says whether it has rows for the country). Mitigation’s section 18 reads both; they feed the Pigouvian components and the welfare of section 19. Section 5 (the engineer road model) holds the outputs the transport co-benefits module will read. A standalone transport co-benefits module is planned to supply the values.

title: 4  Data and working practice
text:
4.1 Data
The data the models read, the norms the project works under, and where everything is in the repository.
All data of the project live in the root folder data/ (rebuilt 2026-10-30). The tidy tables are the source of truth; the legacy-compatible workbook is written from them. Code reads the data from there by a path relative to the repository; nothing is copied into the project folders.

title: 4  Data and working practice
text:
4.2 Working in the repository
The project works under written norms (excel_ai/core/NORMS.md). They bind people and AI agents alike; AGENTS.md at the root of the repository routes any AI agent to them. This section summarises the norms that shape the files a reader meets; NORMS.md is the authority.

4.2.1 Files, versions and releases
Where the files are. People open the Master and the activated modules in excel_ai/active_workbooks/ (Section 1.5); the latest unactivated module is excel_ai/<module>/<Name>_latest.xlsx. The released versions of a module workbook are in the module’s releases/ folder as <Name>_v<version>.<ext> (for example excel_ai/mitigation/releases/CPAT-AI-Mitigation_v1.9.55.xlsx). Mitigation, MT, Unified and Distribution keep only their latest release there; Air pollution and Transport co-benefits keep every release; older versions are in git history. The documents:








File
Where
What it is




Legacy_CPAT_Bugs_v<version>.docx
excel_ai/bugs_and_legacy/
The legacy bugs, with every cell-level fix plan


Tracking_Legacy_Bugs_v<version>.xlsx
excel_ai/bugs_and_legacy/
The master list of bugs and issues

The code protocol, vocabularies, variables, output codes and every input

The slide deck: status, how to use it, results (latest copy: docs/presentations/01_CPAT-AI_Overview_latest.pptx; the short pitch: docs/presentations/04_CPAT-AI_Pitch_latest.pptx)


BUGS.md, ISSUES.md, NORMS.md, TODO.md, CAVEATS.md
excel_ai/core/
The bug and issue lists, the rules, the open work, the task log




Older versions of the documents move to excel_ai/bugs_and_legacy/register/releases/ (the deck’s to excel_ai/mitigation/releases/) when a new version is written (excel_ai/core/tools/release.py).
Version numbers. Three parts, <major>.<minor>.<patch> (0.x before a module’s first full release): the last part for fixes and small features, the middle part for structural or methodological change. Mitigation and the Master share a number (1.3.1). Each module with its own builder has its own version line and records which mitigation version it was built from: Distribution 0.5.1 (built from Mitigation 1.3.1), air pollution 0.x. Files released before the change to three parts were renamed; their contents keep the old two-part numbers. The register documents, the tracker and the codes map carry the version of the mitigation prototype they were made with.
One version table per workbook and generated document, in the same columns: version, date, description (with register codes), and the largest regression difference against the previous release.



4.2.2 Checks








Check
When
What it does




Quick check (check_quick.py)
After every change; a few minutes
Structure, names, literals, formula length, a full recalculation with no error cells, the code protocol, the change of every output code against the last release


Paste test (check_paste.py)
Every release
Pastes the live scenario’s column group into further groups, as a user would, and checks that the pasted groups number themselves, show no errors and reproduce the stored results


Full check (check_full.py)
At a major version; several hours
Everything, including the macro tests


Independent recomputation
Within the checks
Python reference models of the power, transport and distribution blocks reproduce the workbook’s numbers



Every increment is a regression test: the new version’s values are compared with the previous release, and every difference is zero or explained in the version table.


4.2.3 Excel written by code
The Excel prototypes are written with openpyxl and recalculated in LibreOffice, so they build and check on Linux and in cloud sessions. Excel 365 is used for review only. The norms set the column layout of every sheet type, a visual style guide (colours, fonts, borders, sections), formula rules (target 90 characters, at most 115; one formula serves a whole block; repeated formulas stored once as shared formulas), copy-paste ability of scenario columns, and lint rules that every file passes before it ships so Excel never shows a repair prompt.


4.2.4 Task completion
Every finished task ends with an entry at the bottom of excel_ai/core/CAVEATS.md, the single record of completed work: the task, its inputs, its outputs and its caveats. Earlier entries may be corrected but not deleted. Open work is listed in excel_ai/core/TODO.md and coded/TODO.md.
Norms follow the lessons. A mistake whose cause could recur ends with a norm and a check that would have caught it, added in the same task.


4.2.5 Methodology and version notes
A methodology describes the method as it is now, for a reader who has never seen an earlier version. Change history goes in separate version notes: the version tables and CAVEATS.md.
